### policy_conflict_scan

The blueprint category is network, with the network_accounting claim in `blueprint/blueprint.yaml`. Every base YAML value equals its blueprint counterpart. Lifecycle creation/amendment/activation/closure, payment return, outage service credits and ancillary fees have separate triggers from the assisted routes. The two visible needs imply a correction/refund route and an unbilled primary invoice route; formal scope comparison remains masked until both freezes. There is one workflow and seven extended policies. All use the same customer's, same-entity active Support holding only to read its tier fraction, never to write Support. Tax source authority, completed export evidence, exact financial-source identity, deduplication and customer signature ownership remain inherited.

Two shared policy defects are demonstrated below: F1 changes chronological source allocation without declaring its replacement; F2 drops exact-source selectors from executable bindings. These are defects of the charter, independent of whether a particular seed activates every discrepancy.

### rule_compute_equivalence

Across the seven policies, the arithmetic uses decimal half-up at final two-place amounts; allowance subtraction precedes the floor and rate; discount acts on the entire subtotal; correction cap precedes negation; refund takes the three-way minimum before its minimum-payout test; acceptance adds contingency only absent eligible promotion; assessed net is acceptance-bounded; net posting is support/max_resources-bounded; tax acts on issued rounded net. All numerical bindings have a verbatim compute_basis quotation in rule (inventory below). The exact-source mismatches in F2 break the two-way correspondence even though quotes exist. The approval predicates, no-posting thresholds and customer-only ownership must also be applied as business eligibility, not inferred from permissive tool bodies.

Each target tool is claimed exactly once. Suffixes are f148f79a, 4dd38821, f88363e7, 11d4a76e, 84b98f50, 9ee25cfe and 645ca35d; no collision, adjacent sequence or common-prefix batch pattern appears. Source artifacts freeze these suffixes. Independent random generation provenance cannot be established from these four artifact classes alone; this is an observation, not a demonstrated business defect. Tool bodies contain only immediate create/update/receipt effects and no prerequisite validation. `assess`/`price` update the selected review, `authorize` files the user acceptance, `credit`/`refund`/`invoice`/`tax` create distinct signed postings. No outside approval or clearing action is fabricated.

### prerequisite_graph

All seven extended policies and the workflow explicitly contain prerequisite lists. Edges point from dependent to prerequisite: refund→credit→assess and tax→invoice→price→authorize. Each is value_input, gates respectively balance, target, issued, assessed, accepted. Their policy_source sentences are literal rule substrings, conditions match those sentences, and resolved_by points to the immediate writer of the named binding. No cycles or cross-route edges exist. The workflow itself has an empty prerequisite list and its internal policy steps supply its chain. Base policies use their own eligibility framework rather than additional problem nodes.

The base section is unchanged. Assessment explicitly replaces the Support-no-price-change sentence and the pricing priority sentence; credit replaces the correction amount disposition sentence and Support restriction; refund replaces the refund limit sentence and Support restriction. Authorization and assessment replace the Support restriction; invoice replaces that restriction, the pricing rounding/tax sentence and tax-gross assembly sentence; tax replaces Support restriction and gross assembly. ### findings

**F1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED: unannounced change from source allocation to monthly reassessment.** Symptom: a charge whose original source is an early export can receive a positive corrected target even when its own quantity is entirely included. Root cause: `network_ext_assess` introduces whole-month aggregation while declaring only discount/Support overrides. Base `network_evt_pricing.rule` says: “Allocate included_quantity across primary meter sources of the same holding and period in interval_start then source_event_id order” and “Only the positive quantity beyond the remaining included allowance is charged.” Base `network_evt_category_meters.rule` says: “An allowance is consumed chronologically by interval_start then source_event_id within the named holding and UTC period” and “Category-specific primary inclusions replace the generic included_quantity where expressly named; they are not added twice.” Extended rule instead says: “For an unresolved rate-error review, sum posted internet_egress meter quantity for the source charge calendar period on this holding” and its quantity binding sums the month. Task 0 has a charge linked to its first 2,500-GB export, while the 10,000-GB allowance covers that source; the extended formula uses 20,000 GB and produces 643.20. The detailed 0 versus 643.20 target and resulting credit difference are demonstrated in `0.md`. No overwrite names either allocation sentence. Affects extended assessment, its base references and task 0 scored correction chain. First revision; no previous finding is being revised.

**F2 — SOURCE-POLICY RED: exact-source prose is broader in compute.** `network_ext_credit.compute_basis.target` says “Read the approved incorrect rate-error review net_amount for that exact source; a pending review is not an approved amount.” Its binding is `SUM('network_events','net_amount',event_type='network_review',status='approved',decision='incorrect',cause='rate_error')`, with no source_event_id. Likewise invoice assessed prose says “Read the approved correct invoice review net_amount for this source bundle; pending or rejected reviews contribute zero”, but assessed sums every primary approved correct review on the holding. No uniqueness condition prohibits older approved reviews for other sources; uniqueness of the current unbilled bundle does not erase historical reviews. Demonstrated same-situation consequence: with the task-0 current original 660 and target 643.20 plus an older unrelated approved incorrect review of 100, exact-source prose yields a -16.80 correction, whereas the binding's target 743.20 yields zero. For the task-1 source with its 2055.45 approved assessment plus an older unrelated approved correct primary review of 100, exact-source prose yields 2055.45 invoice, whereas the binding yields 2155.45 (both below the 6134.40 cap), changing statutory tax from 169.57 to 177.82. These are explicit charter-domain countermodels, not claims that those extra reviews exist in the frozen seeds. Other selector gaps: assessment chooses a pending review's period instead of dereferencing its original charge; credit original omits the prose's posted predicate; tax issued omits the prose's meter/period predicates. Their numeric impact is not asserted on these two worlds. Affects credit target and invoice assessed rule/compute correspondence; both frozen seeds themselves have only the single selected review. First revision.

**O1 — Observation:** the single workflow has four immediate writes including a user write, but its charter object omits explicit `requires_external_wait=false` and `zero_wait_proof` fields. Its order_rationale provides a substantive synchronous rationale. No actual future event is required by either seed; absence of fields alone is not a demonstrated real-world wait.

**O2 — Observation:** permissive tools do not implement all business deduplication or source identity checks. This is not a RED: the policy layer is responsible for deciding prerequisites, and no negative tool case constitutes an additional business rule.

### policy_conflict_scan and override_declarations

Base charter remains identical to the blueprint. The revised assessment now limits its route to a completed monthly aggregate: sole posted primary internet_egress charge, recorded charge quantity and reconciliation equal monthly exports, month ended, unchanged matching current/source tier/commercial attributes, us_east, active for the full month. It explicitly permits the legacy locator to name a contributing export and explicitly replaces three exact base allocation sentences. A separate undeclared invoice portfolio-eligibility override remains and is now demonstrated as F3 below. It was present in revision1 and was missed in that audit; it is not introduced by this rework, and does not reopen F1 or F2.

### rule_compute_equivalence

Every current compute_basis string is a literal rule substring. Assessment/credit/refund first bind the exact latest uniquely-timed pending authorization, then its review/source or payment. Assessment obtains period from the posted charge. Credit original now requires posted, target fixes both exact review and exact charge with approved/incorrect/rate_error predicates, and prior explicitly sums only correction credit/debit adjustment event types. Refund principal fixes posted ACH payment and used principal events fix the same payment. Invoice-cycle policies fix a uniquely-timed review, its exact posted primary internet_egress bundle, and that bundle's own period; quantity selects that source. Accepted ceiling fixes both source and review with a sole-acceptance route restriction. Invoice assessed fixes exact review/source/approved/correct. Tax issued includes exact source, period, meter, subtype, component and posted status. These selectors now correspond to their prose. Caps, floors, final rounding points and formulas otherwise remain unchanged.

Local in-memory Decimal recomputation over masked seeds, with explicit copies for counterexamples, is recorded in `revision_2_calculation_evidence.json` (SHA256 `037113c8873a3bdd5e58ecd13ad1f6b5dee8ebe981755da75b6b52a267259535`). No actual account tool or external transaction ran. Results: old unrelated approved review100 now leaves task0 credit-16.80 and task1 invoice2055.45 unchanged; a review's altered period does not displace its source's August period; an added wrong-meter charge does not enter the tax base. The calculator uses only current structured bindings, masked records and blueprint tier parameters; current GT was not an input.
